items.prompt: A binary-power proof regroups products of A. Which statement is sufficient without claiming arbitrary matrices commute?

options.why: Associativity groups repeated products; the invariant keeps result*base^remaining in that order.
General matrices need not commute; the lesson explicitly avoids this claim.

options.text: Each cell can be powered independently.
options.why: Elementwise powers do not implement matrix multiplication.
The algorithm supports singular matrices and does not take an inverse.
